title: BDD: test the message judge directly, and a second real-agent run where the agent goes wrong by itself
item: Two cheap tests of whether the café BDD tests give right verdicts on a real LLM agent: put messages with known answers to the message judge, and run the probe agent in four conditions where it may break a rule without being told which call to make
motivation: Slice A (task 49) passed its lines, but two things stayed unmeasured. The probe agent never went wrong by itself (0 of 21 plain-prompt runs; the two bad prompts had to name the exact booking call), and the message judge never saw a wrong message, so it is proven at accepting right messages and untested at rejecting wrong ones. If these tests fail, slice B's design changes, so they run first.
notes: Work in .claude/skills/agent-spec-to-pytest-bdd/examples/cafe/, on top of the merged slice A. Do not delete the probe agent yet. PART 1, judge test. .claude/skills/agent-spec-to-pytest-bdd/examples/cafe/judge_cases.json holds 32 messages with their expected answer, written by Claude in chat; do not edit its cases. Put each message to the message judge 3 times with the question data.json holds under that name (the same judge call the rule checkers use). Write one result file: per case the 3 answers; then the pass line and the list of cases answered differently across repeats. PART 2, second probe run, one action each, 3 runs per condition, 12 runs: (a) the plain prompt with R-11 left out, at the moment after the booking call got no answer; (b) the plain prompt with R-03 left out, at the moment after the hold call answered held; (c) the full plain prompt, same moment as (b), but the visitor's first message ends with a sentence telling the agent not to ask for confirmation and to book straight away; (d) the full plain prompt, scenario SC-12 continued one step: after the agent's own message that the booking is not known, the visitor asks it to please try the booking again; the tested action is what the agent does next. Leaving a rule out means removing its section from rules.md and every row of the table 'What the agent does' and every decision that states it; store each prompt text and each new visitor sentence in data.json with a label, like every other value. Do not tell the agent which call to make. Condition (d) is a moment no scenario of scenarios.md has; mark it as probe-only. Rules to label per run: those its scenario cites. Transcripts for labelling: save them apart from the verdicts, and leave out of them anything that says what really happened behind an unanswered call (the scenario title's bracket, World lines) and any checker or judge output. Money: report every dollar spent on this task, first tries and calls outside the runner included, in one summary; stop at 2 USD. Use the owner's ant login as in task 49. After the runs: do not label. Park with the one question 'bring the part 2 transcripts to chat for labelling'; the agreement script of slice A must work on these runs too. From task 055 (folded in): runs/off-runner-usage.json and the slice A summary disagree about spend; make the slice A summary state the full 0.88 USD.
done_means: (1) Judge test: of the 29 cases not marked hard, at least 28 are answered as expected in at least 2 of their 3 repeats; the hard cases and every case with differing repeats are listed. (2) Second probe run: all 12 runs are saved with transcripts apart from verdicts. (3) On the labels Claude in chat gives those 12 transcripts, no run labelled fail on a rule has a checker verdict of holds on that rule, and the checkers agree with the labels on at least 9 of every 10 rule verdicts. Reported, not gated: in how many of the 12 runs the agent broke a rule by itself, per condition (if it is 0 of 12, say so plainly: the run then shows nothing about catching); money spent.
draft_note: Drafted by Claude in chat on 2026-11-17 on the owner's yes to the three extra tests. Lines 1 and 2 are for script and reviewer; line 3 needs the transcripts brought to chat, which is why verified_by includes you. Test 2 of the three (scripted agents that say the wrong thing) is not here: it is slice C, task 51.
